subject: Dispute: Partial degradation on 2026-02-12 and request for service credit (Atlas Payments)
messages:
From: Jordan Li <jordan.li@atlaspayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: status@atlaspayments.com
Date: 2026-02-12 15:07 PST
Subject: Partial degradation 2026-02-12 — request for credit

Hi Marissa,

We observed a sustained increase in 5xx errors and request latency between ~09:42–10:35 UTC on 12 Feb for the payment-validation route served via your hosted API. Our telemetry shows ~48 minutes where tail latency frequently exceeded 6s and about ~15% of requests returned 500. We collected request samples and are attaching a small set (atlas_error_samples.json).

Per section 4.2 of our SLA, Atlas is eligible for service credits when the effective uptime for a billing period drops below the 99.9% target. Redwood's initial status page posted an incident marked as "partial degradation" and referenced a third-party CDN outage. Atlas believes the impact we saw should count toward the downtime window because requests did not failover gracefully and our user-facing flows were impacted.

We'd like to request (a) a detailed timeline showing Redwood's incident boundaries versus the third-party outage, (b) an explanation of why those 48 minutes are being excluded from credit calculation if that is your position, and (c) the formal service credit calculation per our contract.

We need a resolution by EOD Monday (02/15). Can you confirm receipt and next steps?

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Platform Ops
Atlas Payments

---
Attachment: atlas_error_samples.json (JSON, 12 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Hi Jordan — thanks for the samples and for raising this quickly. Confirmed receipt. I'm escalating to our incident review team (cc'd).

Immediate next steps from our side:
- We'll compile a precise incident timeline comparing Redwood ingress/routing metrics with the third-party CDN's outage window.
- We'll look for any service-level regressions on our side (routing failures, KV cache evictions, model fallback not being triggered).
- We expect an initial update within 24 hours and a formal credit proposal within 48 hours.

A couple of quick clarifications that will speed our review: did Atlas observe any client-side retries or traffic spike correlated with load-testing in your environment at that time? Also confirming the most affected route is /v1/predict/payment-validate (as noted).

Marissa

Redwood Inference

Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-13 13:45 PST
Subject: Re: Partial degradation 2026-02-12 — request for credit

Jordan — we've completed an initial correlation and wanted to share interim findings before the full RCA. Attached is our incident timeline that overlays Redwood ingress success/error rates, CDN provider incident window, and our internal routing logs. High-level takeaways:

- The third-party CDN reported an outage window from 09:35–10:20 UTC.
- Redwood's upstream metrics show elevated error rates starting at 09:40 UTC and normalizing by ~10:40 UTC.
- We observed a configuration rollback on our routing layer at 09:46 UTC that caused ~6 minutes where fallback routing rules did not apply as intended. That 6-minute window produced the highest concentration of 5xxs.

Per our SLA (section 5, Exceptions), incidents attributed solely to third-party providers are excluded from uptime calculations unless Redwood's controls failed to trigger the contractual fallbacks. Given the routing rollback we observed, there's a small segment where Redwood bears responsibility. For the remainder of the window, the root cause appears to be the CDN provider.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Formal credit calculation limited to the minutes where Redwood routing rollback is the proximate cause (we're preparing the SLO math).
2) A goodwill credit to acknowledge customer impact while we refine fallbacks (details below).
3) A joint RCA meeting next week to walk through logs and mitigations.

I'll follow up with priyom and Rafael who will finalize the SLO calculation and a proposed credit amount.

Marissa

---
Attachment: redwood_incident_timeline.pdf (PDF, 210 KB)
Attachment: slo_calculation.csv (CSV, 6 KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14 10:30 PST
Subject: Redwood assessment and credit proposal — Atlas Payments incident 2026-02-12

Jordan / Marissa — following our analysis and the timeline Marissa shared, here is the technical/calc summary and formal credit proposal. Apologies for the detail, but I wanted to be explicit so the calculations map back to contract language.

Summary of facts:
- Third-party CDN outage window (provider): 2026-02-12 09:35–10:20 UTC (provider status page).
- Redwood ingress error/latency elevation: 2026-02-12 09:40–10:40 UTC (our metrics).
- Confirmed routing configuration rollback: 2026-02-12 09:46–09:52 UTC (6 minutes) — this change prevented our fallback policy from diverting traffic to the dedicated hot path.

SLA language applied:
Per section 5 (Exceptions), outages attributable to third-party providers are excluded from the uptime calculation except where Redwood's operational failure (including misapplied routing config rollbacks) is the proximate cause for customer-impacting errors.

Calculation approach:
- Billing period uptime baseline: 99.9% (monthly).
- We measured total customer-impacting downtime for the event: 58 minutes (09:40–10:38 UTC approximate).
- We assign attribution: 6 minutes (100%) to Redwood (routing rollback), remaining 52 minutes (100%) to CDN provider.

Credit proposal:
1) Service credit for the 6-minute segment where Redwood's config rollback is the proximate cause. Per contract formula, this equates to a pro-rated credit for 6/ (30 days * 24 * 60) of monthly fees = ~0.014% of monthly host fees (mathematical conversion included in attached PDF).
2) Goodwill credit: we recognize the broader customer impact and propose an additional one-time account credit equal to 10% of the monthly host fees for the affected product, payable against next invoice, in lieu of contesting the remaining third-party-attributed minutes. This is above-and-beyond contractual minimum and intended to accelerate resolution.

Operational mitigations we will enact immediately:
- Audit routing config rollback protections and add a preflight check for rollback changes to avoid accidental removal of fallback rules.
- Add an automated test that simulates CDN failures and validates model fallback triggers end-to-end.
- Offer to run a joint runbook validation with Atlas during a mutually scheduled window.

Attachments: credit_proposal.pdf (breakdown and math), incident_config_diff.txt (diff of routing config showing rollback).

If this proposal is acceptable we will start processing the credit and schedule the RCA meeting. Otherwise please propose an alternative and we'll revisit.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: credit_proposal.pdf (PDF, 24 KB)
Attachment: incident_config_diff.txt (TXT, 3 KB)

Marissa / Rafael — thanks for the clear breakdown and the goodwill offer. Atlas accepts the proposed combined credit (contract prorated amount for the 6-minute attribution + 10% goodwill credit against next invoice). Two requests before you process: (1) can you expedite the credit so it appears on the next invoice cycle, and (2) we'd like the RCA meeting scheduled in the next 5 business days.

Separately, Atlas legal will follow up about tightening SLA language around third-party exclusions to ensure clearer attribution rules. We'll send proposed edits.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Jordan
